Quote: brickman, Nov 24 2004, 05:34 PM
Except for telling the game which sprite, which way its facing, nd what its rotation is. Remember, the way flash works, n running up a slope is the same sprite as n running on flat ground, only rotated (thats why they chose flash), and when he runs the other way its the same sprite but flipped, so a minimum of three extra things for it to check (sprite, rotation, left or right) in addition to his exact coordinates. Vs with a dot, its only one sprite which needs no flipping or rotating, thus only coords must be checked each frame.

I don't think thats a problem. Checking N's rotation and direction aswell as his x and y isn't exactly intensive. But then again, my Flash knowledge is about as limited as a one-armed man dangling off a cliff

Quote: Arachnid, Jan 8 2005, 05:24 AM
Don't rely on these too much, because it's not tested thoroughly yet. I extracted this from the BNF definitions in the RFC for URLs (argh, acronym overload). Written for use with preg_*:
%(http://(?:[-0-9a-z]*(?:\.[-0-9a-z]*)+|[0-9]
{1,3}(?:\.[0-9]{1,3}){3})(?:\:[0-9]+)?(?:/[-a-zA-Z0-9
;:@&=._]*)*(?:\?[-a-zA-Z0-9;:@&=._]*)?)%
Thanks, it seems to work pretty well :thumbsup:

#55499 7 2005-03-23T09:43:37Z trib4lmaniac
Quote: Daddaluma, Mar 23 2005, 04:21 AM
So I went digging on the adblock forum and found a little bit of adblock code that I don't understand but worked: /[^a-zA-Z]ads*/

That's a regular expression. The two slashes ( / ) are caled delimeters, which mark the start and end of the expression. The [^a-zA-Z] means not any letter of the alphabet (the caret means not). "ads" is a literal block of text. And the aterix means anything (a wildcard).

/[^a-zA-Z]ads*/ altogether will block anything that matches that pattern.

.adsgalore - blocked
badslaughter - not blocked
ads - not blocked
%ads% - blocked

You get the idea

Quote: Eldrial, Mar 30 2005, 03:58 AM
i'm catholic, and wut i find a little strange is that we [the catholics which also includes christians....cuz they're basicly mostly the same] celebrate jesus's resurrection w/ bunnies and chocalate.  strange?  i think so! 
The eggs and bunnies have pagan origins I think. I can't remember the details though.

*looks it up*

Quote
Pagan Practices That Were Christianized

  Easter Eggs: Since the eating of eggs was formerly forbidden during Lent, decorated eggs, claims The Encyclopedia Americana, could symbolize the end of the penitential season and the beginning of joyful celebration. However, reference works agree that the egg was a symbol of life and fertility among idolaters. Says the book Celebrations: Eggs were said to be dyed and eaten at the spring festivals in ancient Egypt, Persia, Greece, and Rome. The Persians of that time gave eggs as gifts at the vernal equinox.

  Easter Hares and Rabbits: In Europe, the hare has long been a traditional symbol of Easter. (In North America, the animal is a rabbita close relative of the hare.) Yet The New Encyclopdia Britannica explains that the hare was the symbol of fertility in ancient Egypt. Thus when children hunt for Easter eggs, supposedly brought by the Easter rabbit, this is not mere childs play, but the vestige of a fertility rite.Funk & Wagnalls Standard Dictionary of Folklore, Mythology and Legend, volume 1, page 335.

  Sunrise Services: Says The Book of Festivals and Holidays the World Over: It was a common belief among the early Christians that on Easter morning the sun danced in honor of the Resurrection and people rose long before the sun to see the feat. Perhaps this ancient belief is the inspiration for the many sunrise services that take place on Easter morning in all parts of the United States and Europe.

  But says Walshs Curiosities of Popular Customs: This idea of the sun dancing on Easter Day may easily be traced back to heathen customs, when the spectators themselves danced at a festival in honor of the sun, after the vernal equinox.

  The book Celebrations adds: Sunrise services are not unrelated to the Easter fires held on the tops of hills in continuation of the New Year fires, a worldwide observance in antiquity. Rites were performed at the vernal equinox welcoming the sun and its great power to bring new life to all growing things.

  Water Rites: The belief that running water on Easter morning is especially blessed is common. However, Hastings Encyclopdia of Religion and Ethics reminds us: Since water is one of the essential factors in the preservation of life and the growth of the crops, it naturally plays a conspicuous part in rainmaking ceremonies and other seasonal rites among primitive people.

  The Blessing of the New Fire: A Catholic rite, in preparation for the Easter vigil, in which a fire is started from a flint rock. Says Hastings Encyclopdia of Religion and Ethics: The new fire probably took rise from a pagan custom to which, when adopted by Christians, a gospel symbolism was attached.
Even the word "Easter" is derived from the name of a pagan god (Eostre).

Why? Because the game is meant to be played, guys, not to be handed out by trib4l. And I'll be damned if I'll sit here and let you guys ruin the entire point of the game just because people don't have the patience to get past a couple of the levels. Pretty soon, every newb who can't get past 5-2 will come running to everyone else, looking for handouts, and that isn't gonna happen so long as I'm here. Ya'll can do it outside of here, but it ain't happenin' here. It took me a hell of a long time to beat the game. Why? Because I'm absolutely awful at N. But I kept plugging away when I was stuck, and that's how others should do it, too. That's the entire point of the game, guys - to play. Yes, it's a hard game. Yes, it's frustrating as hell, but no, trib4l isn't finishing people's games. Particularly when these people have been playing less than a month. You can't realistically expect to be good at N after only such a short time playing. Ya know what levels these guys are stuck on? The early ones. The magic and charm and beauty of N lies in the experience, and I'm not going to let that go to hell. Ya know what the best part of N was for me? After spending an entire week on MTI, I finally beat it. And it was the most satisfying thing in the world for me. I don't really care much that it took me an entire week of neglecting myself and sitting at my computer 10 hours a day, but after the literally thousands of tries, I beat it, and it was one of the greatest gaming accomplishments in my life. To beat some of these levels took me days, weeks, and months, insane levels of frustration and heartache, but it was all worth it.

For you, I'm ashamed that you would so readily hand out .sols like candy, when you know full well, just like I do, that these players haven't tried to beat these levels like we have. THAT is why.

I'm not planning on completing peoples games for them! The only sol I've given out with more than 2 levels beaten is to The Daily Llama, because I trust him when he says he got as far as he did. But banning the sharing of sol files just because you aren't happy with people getting something for nothing is not right IMO. It's a free world, and I hope most people on these forums are sensible enough to use their ninja skills with descretion.

Quote: Keron Cyst, Jun 22 2005, 06:51 AM
Interesting. Any section following an & that the URL provider doesn't understand is ignored, but keeps the link still working?

Anything after the ? is called "Get data." (In PHP at least, ) These usually come in pairs...

myurl.com/index.php?key=value&another_key=another_value&so=on&so=forth

So Eeyores still has the important two keys with the correct value to make the link log you out (act=Login and CODE=03) and also sends the key n_v14b_userdata.sol which is equal to... nothing. As the page doesnt check for it's existance - because it's never heard of it - it is ignored.

Quote: Readme.txt
-= USER LEVELS MODE =-

You can now play custom levels in N's game mode -- just click on User Levels from N's main menu.  You'll
see a list displaying your current collection of custom levels.  Clicking on entries in the list loads the
level so you can play it immediately.  Click on a column heading ("level name", "author", etc.) to sort levels
by that column.


Included in your N download is a .txt file called userlevels.txt.  This file contains all the user level data
which will be loaded into the game.  We've started it with a sampling of our favourite user maps which didn't
make it into N1.4.  When you add your own levels and levels you've downloaded from NUMA to this text file,
they'll appear on the list you see in User Levels mode. 


*** EXTREMELY IMPORTANT ***
DO NOT DELETE userlevels.txt!!


View the instructions in userlevels.txt for more information on adding and organising user maps.


User Levels mode also features a way for you to save and share replay data. 
After you play a level and return to the user levels menu, the replay will be available in a textbox
on the left side of the screen.  You'll have to manually copy and paste the data to a text file,
but this new feature allows you to swap game mode replays with other N players.

User Levels records personal bests as well -- not for highscores, but to indicate that you've
beaten a user level, and to allow you to replay your best run at any time.  If you've beaten a user
level, a button will appear beside its entry in the list of levels.  Click the button to watch your
personal best replay. As usual, the replay data will be available in the textbox to the left of the list.
